text:
Casey (sales): Quick sync — Medixia POC. They want steady ~150 qps chat (avg ~40 tokens/resp) + search embeddings that can spike to ~500 qps for short windows. Asking: recommended reserved GPU commit, how burst credits apply, and autoscale behavior during spikes / AZ failover. Any blockers from security questionnaire? @Toni to confirm ask

Toni (solutions): They need dedicated capacity (compliance) and an initial 3-week POC. Attached workload trace (small csv) — spikes are ~2–3x for 2–5min every 6 hours. Also they prefer quantized LLM variants where feasible.

Matt (eng-runtime): Quick calc: 150 qps * 40 tokens = 6k tokens/sec (~360k tokens/min) steady. Spikes to 500 qps for embeddings are separate (embeds are faster per token but CPU-bound). For chat throughput, on our current db-standard A100-like profile, a single GPU can sustain ~220–260 qps for short responses if KV cache warm. But with cold KV and 40-token median we'd plan lower. My recommendation: reserve 2 GPUs as baseline + allow 2 additional burst GPUs (burst credits) for spikes.

Olivia (sre): +1 on reserve 2, but we should set autoscale min=2, max=4, and a cooldown window of 120s. Also preheat KV cache on traffic ramps. If they have AZ affinity requirement, recommend cross-AZ placement of those 2 baseline GPUs to avoid single-AZ blast.

Casey (sales): Sounds reasonable. How do burst credits get consumed? Do they bill extra if we use burst GPUs?

Matt (eng-runtime): Burst credits are a billing construct for short-term capacity above commit. For POC we can allow usage under trial burst bucket (no extra immediate cost) but for enterprise commit we suggest a blended price: reserved GPUs cover baseline, burst usage billed at a higher per-minute rate. I'll ask pricing to give a two-line quote.

Evan (security): Security questionnaire stuff — Medixia flagged KMS + audit log retention (7 years). Private deployment wanted? They said VPC peering might be acceptable. If they insist on on-prem, that changes capacity advice.

Toni (solutions): They said VPC is fine for POC; on-prem was exploratory. KMS + 7y logs — ops + security will need to confirm retention options.

Olivia (sre): Operational runbook notes: 1) Preheat windows: run KV-warmup 3m before expected spike if schedule known. 2) Canary policy: route 5% traffic to new model + ramp over 10m. 3) On AZ failover, traffic will shift to remaining GPUs; if we lose one baseline GPU and had min=2 cross-AZ, consider immediate temporary increase to burst to avoid 429s.

Matt (eng-runtime): Sample autoscale snippet for handoff to ops (paste into config):

```
autoscale:
  min: 2
  max: 4
  target_qps_per_gpu: 180
  cooldown_seconds: 120
  burst_behavior: allow_burst_while_preheating
  kv_preheat: true
```

Casey (sales): Perfect — can you also call out expected tail latency impact during cold starts? Medixia worries about 95th pct.

Matt (eng-runtime): Cold starts can add 300–800ms per request depending on model variant; if KV cold it's more for long context. With preheat + prefix cache we expect 95p within SLA (~400ms) for chat after warm. For embeddings spikes it's mostly throughput; expect <200ms p95 if CPU isn't saturated.

Evan (security): For the questionnaire we can confirm: VPC peering, KMS support, audit logs (we support exports to S3/BigQuery with retention controls). I'll draft answers and ping legal for retention beyond default.

Casey (sales): Action items: 1) Matt — provide a short two-line hardware + autoscale recommendation for the quote. 2) Evan — draft security questionnaire replies for KMS/logs and share. 3) Olivia — ops runbook bullet points + preheat checklist. 4) Toni — confirm POC dates and attach workload trace.

ops-bot: Reminder: create ticket #POC-7821 for Medixia onboarding (assigned: Toni).

Toni (solutions): I'll schedule the POC kickoff for next Tue, share trace, and confirm they accept 2 baseline GPUs + burst.

Casey (sales): Thanks team — will update Medixia with recommended commit + that security + ops are aligning. :thumbsup:
